result.rationale: The diff shows parseRefreshTokenResponse setting `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when absent, and Office365CalendarService then spreads `tokenResponse.data` over o365AuthCredentials and persists via `prisma.credential.update`, so a response lacking refresh_token (which the new minimumTokenResponseSchema allows under the sharing path) would overwrite the real refresh token with a literal placeholder string, breaking future refreshes. Mechanism verified directly in the diff.

judged_text: When the parsed data lacks refresh_token, the function writes the literal string "refresh_token" into data.refresh_token — a placeholder, not a token — and callers persist it. Under the sharing path the broken minimum schema always strips refresh_token, so Office365CalendarService spreads {refresh_token: "refresh_token"} over o365AuthCredentials and prisma persists it, permanently destroying the real Microsoft refresh token and forcing every affected user to reconnect; zoom's refreshed credential is corrupted the same way, and any provider response that legitimately omits refresh_token now corrupts the stored credential instead of preserving the old value as the previous spread-only code did.
